about: Lessons, reflections, counts, notes and lessons_md are real: harness.learning.views run over out/memory-fake.json in the memory worktree (sam/memory 917e3b2), read only. Procedures and outcomes are synthesized (no harness.db has a review edit or recorded metric yet), built through the real EditPair, edit_diff and views.procedure_rows.

GET /api/memory.lessons_md:
# Lessons

Generated by `python -m harness learn` from lessons that passed a held-out test. Don't edit by hand.

(No tested lessons yet.)

action.text: Fever fans: favorite Clark moment of the season? Mine's the fourth-quarter logo three against Seattle.
Shoutout to the Iowa fans who drove four hours to Indy tonight.
Sky fans really thought they had a rivalry. Respectfully, check the box scores since May.
Clark pulling up from the Gainbridge logo like it's a free throw 😭
That logo three was a statement. Sky had no answer all night.
Fever are 11-3 when Clark and Boston both score 15+. That's the season in one stat.
Caitlin Clark has 19 games with 10+ assists this season, the most by any guard in a single WNBA season.

lessons.text: Lead with the concrete news and include the specific detail, such as the name, number or feature.
lessons.evidence_sentence: trait on 13 of 21 held-out successes vs 6 of 21 failures from the same accounts
lessons.tested_as: Does the post announce a specific new thing, such as a rename, a funding or credits amount, a launched page or feature, or an event recap, with concrete details in the text?
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded
likely launch-confounded: it describes announcements, and launches get paid and bot boosts that the launch keyword rule doesn't fully catch

lessons.text: Attach a video or image to posts that promote a link instead of posting text and link alone.
lessons.evidence_sentence: trait on 14 of 21 held-out failures vs 8 of 21 successes from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded

lessons.text: Attach a short demo video to technical or event posts instead of posting a bare link.
lessons.evidence_sentence: trait on 20 of 60 held-out successes vs 6 of 81 failures from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded

lessons.text: State the actual news or result in the post text rather than only pointing readers to a link.
lessons.evidence_sentence: trait on 13 of 21 held-out failures vs 6 of 21 successes from the same accounts
lessons.tested_as: Is the post mostly a vague pointer to a link (e.g. 'read more', 'RSVP', 'more on our blog') without stating a specific fact, number or result?
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded

reflections.claim: Posts about third parties or culture (hotel shout-out with hiring pitch, external blocklist news) rather than the product's own capability fail, even with a photo.
reflections.predicate: Is the post about a third party, venue or external news rather than something the account's own product does or offers?
reflections.tested_as: Is the post about a third party, venue or external news rather than something the account's own product does or offers?
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 10 of 81 held-out failures vs 6 of 60 successes from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded

reflections.claim: Very short posts that are only a generic call to action plus a link (or an emoji plus a link) fail. They give no reason to click, and they come from the same accounts whose longer, specific posts did well.
reflections.predicate: Is the post a bare link drop of under about 60 characters with a generic prompt like 'Watch the full talk', 'Register' or 'Try it here', or just an emoji?
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 20 of 83 held-out failures vs 13 of 61 successes from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded

reflections.claim: Posts announcing something new or concrete from the product (new regions, a new product, an open-sourced tool, a new framework integration, benchmark results) succeed. They state specific news or a benefit and often invite people to try it.
reflections.predicate: Does the post announce a specific new product, feature, release or result, or invite people to try something new?
reflections.tested_as: Does the post announce a specific new product, feature, release or result, or invite people to try something new?
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 28 of 61 held-out successes vs 31 of 83 failures from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded
likely launch-confounded: it describes announcements, and launches get paid and bot boosts that the launch keyword rule doesn't fully catch

reflections.claim: Failures are mid-thread or minor-update posts that assume context: a '2/' continuation, a mention-led 'new installation page', or a credit for a tool. The text doesn't say why a casual reader should care. Successes are standalone or a thread opener with a hook.
reflections.predicate: Is the post a mid-thread continuation or a minor update/credit that depends on outside context to matter?
reflections.tested_as: Is the post a mid-thread continuation or a minor update/credit that depends on outside context to matter?
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 10 of 81 held-out failures vs 8 of 60 successes from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded

reflections.claim: Posts that announce something concrete and new, with specifics such as a new name, a dollar amount, a new page, or an event recap, succeed. They offer a clear stake that a generic link or a testimonial doesn't.
reflections.predicate: Does the post announce a specific new thing, such as a rename, a funding or credits amount, a launched page or feature, or an event recap, with concrete details in the text?
reflections.tested_as: Does the post announce a specific new thing, such as a rename, a funding or credits amount, a launched page or feature, or an event recap, with concrete details in the text?
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 28 of 61 held-out successes vs 12 of 83 failures from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded
likely launch-confounded: it describes announcements, and launches get paid and bot boosts that the launch keyword rule doesn't fully catch

reflections.claim: Posts that open with an @mention, such as replies to partners or users that mostly hand over links, fail. The successes in these groups are all standalone broadcasts.
reflections.predicate: Does the post start with an @mention?
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 3 of 83 held-out failures vs 0 of 61 successes from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded

reflections.claim: Successful posts open with a bold, concrete claim or capability change, with a specific number or feature, such as 500x lower tail latency, pnpm with no node_modules, or Muse making apps in Replit.
reflections.predicate: Does the post open by stating a specific new capability, number, or feature change?
reflections.tested_as: Does the post open by stating a specific new capability, number, or feature change?
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 20 of 60 held-out successes vs 12 of 81 failures from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded

reflections.claim: Failures are generic pointers to a link (read more, RSVP, more on our blog) with no concrete news or detail in the text; the reader has to click to learn what it is. Successes state the news, story, or result in the post itself.
reflections.predicate: Is the post mostly a vague pointer to a link (e.g. 'read more', 'RSVP', 'more on our blog') without stating a specific fact, number or result?
reflections.tested_as: Is the post mostly a vague pointer to a link (e.g. 'read more', 'RSVP', 'more on our blog') without stating a specific fact, number or result?
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 38 of 81 held-out failures vs 12 of 60 successes from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded

reflections.claim: Failures are bare link-only or generic call-to-action posts ("Watch the full talk", "Register today") with no concrete news, name or detail in the text and no media. Successes state what is happening and who is involved.
reflections.predicate: Is the post text just a generic call to action or a bare link (e.g. 'Watch the full talk', 'Register today') with no specific names, numbers or features?
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 23 of 81 held-out failures vs 11 of 60 successes from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded

reflections.claim: Event and ticket promotion posts (early bird deadlines, speaker announcements, last-chance ticket sales) fail, even with a photo or video.
reflections.predicate: Does the post promote an event or push readers to buy a ticket before a deadline?
reflections.tested_as: text contains any of ticket, Early bird, early bird, Builder's Day, Builder’s Day
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 8 of 83 held-out failures vs 0 of 61 successes from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded

reflections.claim: Successes include a human story, community event, or a clear stance or clarification, giving emotional or social interest beyond the product.
reflections.predicate: Does the post tell a story about people or take a clear stance or clarification?
reflections.tested_as: Does the post tell a story about people or take a clear stance or clarification?
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 13 of 60 held-out successes vs 12 of 81 failures from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded
likely launch-confounded: it describes announcements, and launches get paid and bot boosts that the launch keyword rule doesn't fully catch

reflections.claim: In Expo and Modal, every video post succeeded, while the failures in those groups were text-only link drops. Video seems to lift engagement where plain link posts fail.
reflections.predicate: Does the post include a video?
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 19 of 61 held-out successes vs 8 of 83 failures from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded

reflections.claim: Posts that are just a short label plus a bare link, with no hook, claim or reason to click, get almost no engagement.
reflections.predicate: Is the post only a short label or phrase followed by a link, with no substantive claim, hook or explanation?
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 24 of 83 held-out failures vs 18 of 61 successes from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded

reflections.claim: Text-only posts with no link and no media fail. Examples are a customer quote, a security-review paragraph and an apology. They offer no action or visual hook. Every success in these groups includes a link.
reflections.predicate: Is the post text-only, with no link and no media?
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 7 of 83 held-out failures vs 6 of 61 successes from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded

reflections.claim: Posts announcing a new product capability or integration, with a named feature and a short video, succeed (Crush, Warp, Resend webhooks). Failures lack a feature announcement.
reflections.predicate: Does the post announce a new product feature or integration and include a video?
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 20 of 60 held-out successes vs 6 of 81 failures from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded
likely launch-confounded: it describes announcements, and launches get paid and bot boosts that the launch keyword rule doesn't fully catch

reflections.claim: Event follow-up and recap posts (watch the full talk or discussion) get little engagement, while event promotion that names speakers and companies with a video succeeds.
reflections.predicate: Is the post a recap or replay link for a past event or talk without naming speakers or highlights?
reflections.tested_as: Is the post a recap or replay link for a past event or talk without naming speakers or highlights?
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 1 of 81 held-out failures vs 1 of 60 successes from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded

reflections.claim: Replit failures are text-only link posts, while successes carry video or photo media. Bare-link text posts with no media underperform.
reflections.predicate: Is the post's media 'none' and does it include a link?
reflections.evidence_sentence: trait on 58 of 81 held-out failures vs 25 of 60 successes from the same accounts
caveats: boost flags were unavailable, so boosted successes were not excluded
